key_insight: Multi-turn, adaptive red-teaming can reliably breach safety-critical LLM agent defenses, and the main risk is not a single universally weak model but near-disjoint vulnerabilities across models.
engineering_relevance: For safety-critical control rooms and similar supervisory systems, robustness must be evaluated under sustained adversarial interaction, because a defense that helps one model may hurt another.
method: Built NRT-Bench for multi-turn red-teaming of LLM agent teams in a simulated nuclear power plant control room.
Used a five-role operator team with four adversarial channels, per-turn feedback, and objective harm defined by loss of a critical safety function.
Evaluated four frontier operator models with paired replay attacks and optional defense stacks/assistant agents.
evidence_signal: Across four models, 8.7%–12.1% of attack sessions caused loss of a critical safety function, and in 149 sessions no attack defeated all four models while about one-third defeated at least one.
watch_item: Results come from a simulated venue and a fixed-attack replay setup, so real-world transfer and defense effects may differ under live, adaptive operations.
paper_title: LLM agent safety, multi-turn red-teaming, jailbreak benchmarks, adversarial robustness, safety-critical systems
